title: Surge protection: cluster quarantine, regional fencing, and rolling-upgrade safety for Dedicated control planes
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a surge-protection subsystem for Dedicated and Private control planes that can quickly quarantine misbehaving clusters/tenants, apply region-aware fencing, and provide rolling-upgrade safety with multi-tiered circuit breakers and adaptive load-shedding rules. The goal is to preserve global SLOs and minimize blast radius during traffic spikes or problematic upgrades.
background: Incidents in Dedicated customers during the last two quarters exposed two recurring failure modes: 1) a single tenant or upgrade causing cascading resource exhaustion across a control plane pool; 2) regional failover that amplifies load into remaining capacity and causes a second-wave outage. Existing admission controllers and tenant-scoped throttles are insufficient for fast quarantine and safe rollouts at scale.
goals: Provide an automated cluster quarantine action that isolates a misbehaving node/pod-group within 30s of detection
Introduce region-aware fencing so that traffic can be diverted without overloading adjacent regions
Implement multi-level circuit breakers (tenant, cluster, region) with configurable thresholds tied to latency and error SLOs
Support rolling-upgrade safety by proactively pausing or throttling upgrades when downstream SLO risk is elevated
Expose observability to operators and customers (per-tenant SLO impact, quarantine events, degraded mode traces)
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine workflow can be triggered automatically by SRE rules and manually via Console; quarantine completes end-to-end in < 45s in testing
Circuit breakers trip at configured percentiles (p99 latency or error rate) and fallback routes are exercised in canary tests
Region fencing policy successfully prevents failover storms in the staged chaos scenarios in the test harness
Rolling-upgrade job halts when global SLO risk > 2x baseline, with automatic resume after mitigation and operator confirmation
Runbook updated and validated in a tabletop drill with on-call and solutions engineering
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design): define quarantine object schema, fence/route metadata, and CB thresholds (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (runtime): implement durable quarantine controller + lightweight per-tenant admission token bucket and CB hooks (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (networking): add region-aware fence actions to the router to redirect traffic to fallback clusters or degrade to CPU-only runtime (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (upgrade safety): integrate with rollout manager to pause/rollback on SLO regressions and expose upgrade gating in Console (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (test & rollout): staged canary across 3 customers, automated chaos tests, and progressive ramp for Dedicated pools (2 weeks)
risks: Over-aggressive quarantine could unnecessarily reduce capacity for healthy tenants — mitigated by staged canary and conservative default thresholds
Incorrect region fencing rules may cause loops or blackholes — will add validation and simulation harness
Telemetries not granular enough to make fast decisions — telemetry contract defined as part of Phase 1
observability_requirements: Per-tenant SLI stream (latency, error, tokens/sec) with 1s granularity for CB decisions
Audit events for quarantine actions and operator overrides retained for 90 days
Console panels: active quarantines, per-region capacity headroom, upgrade gating status
testing_plan: Unit tests for quarantine controller state transitions
Integration tests: simulate tenant spike -> quarantine -> traffic reroute
Chaos test: simulate region outage + failover storm; measure SLO preservation
Canary runbook: 3-customer progressive rollout with automated rollback on SLO regression
rollout_plan: Internal canary in staging clusters (1 day)
Beta rollout to 3 low-risk Dedicated customers (1 week)
Gradual enable for 20% of Dedicated capacity with monitoring alarms (2 weeks)
Full rollout after 4-week observation window and fixes
